items.description:

items.title: Peru, already home to over 290 lizard species, finds a new one
items.description:
Scientists have discovered a new species of lizard in the Peruvian Andes, the Natural History Museum of San Marcos University said on Saturday.
The lizard measures between six and eight centimetres and has distinct colouration depending on sex.
Females have square-shaped spots on their backs, while males have oblique spots and white scales that help them blend into their rocky surroundings.
The lizard feeds on plants and small arthropods, including spiders, beetles, true bugs and insect larvae.

items.description:

items.title: Trump shares Republican senator's phone number in feud over daylight saving bill
items.description:
US President Donald Trump on Saturday posted the supposed phone number of a Republican US senator online, escalating a feud over daylight saving time.
Trump’s post on Truth Social urged people to call a phone number that he said belonged to Senator Tom Cotton, an Arkansas Republican.
The dispute centres on the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make daylight saving time permanent and end the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks by one hour.
Trump says most Americans want more afternoon sunlight, but Cotton has argued the change would plunge early risers into darkness during winter months

items.title: Fatima Sana joins Perth Scorchers for Women’s Big Bash League
items.description:
Pakistan women’s cricket captain Fatima Sana has signed a one-year contract with Perth Scorchers for the upcoming Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL) season, the Australian club announced on Saturday.
The 24-year-old all-rounder will be available for the Scorchers’ first eight matches of WBBL 12, which begins on Oct 29.
Her stay could be extended if she receives permission from the Pakistan Cricket Board to miss a training camp ahead of the national side’s expected tour of the West Indies in December.
